claim: pw17's E paths ran at 1.45-2.1x the stream because each lane's decode was a serial chain through shared memory. The bake measured about 2,500 clk per unit per warp, against about 1,560 needed and about 800 estimated. Two causes stack: every pair's code length came from an LDS (about 110 clk effective per chained LDS), and the v2 lane-contiguous ring made each refill LDS 12-way (ED 4) or 22-way (ED 8) bank-conflicted, which explains why d8 was slower than single and single slower than rep (codec-study post-mortem). v3 makes three changes. (a) The code length is fixed by the first 3 bits (DP-optimal prefix code, +0.03 bits/weight against Huffman), so the bit-position chain per pair is LOP3, then PRMT, then SHF.R.W: three ALU ops with no memory. The value LUT LDS hangs off the chain and the compiler batches them. (b/c) There are 1, 2 or 4 independent substreams per lane. (d) The ring is [substream][slot][lane] with 4 B pieces, one bank per lane, so it is conflict-free, and refill words are prefetched one step ahead. Expected chain is about 16 x 3 ALU + 4 refills, about 300 clk per unit, so the kernel should run at the HBM stream for 11.07 bits (K1) and pooler m=1 should fall about 1 us below r6. The cost is issue: 256-286 SASS per unit against r6's 49, about 66% of issue at pooler m=1 with 16 warps/SM.
paths: ge-* (gv FMT 4) for qkv_gate, pooler and unpooler at m = 1, 8 and 16 on pw17's geometries: qkv 1.8.16 (m=16 MT2 too), pooler 2.8.16 (512 threads), unpooler 1.4.16 (m <= 8 on rows 0..1023, m=16 XS2). Per (layer, m) there are K1 single LUT (ge-x), K1 lane-replicated (ge-xr), K2 replicated (ge-xr-k2) and K4 replicated (ge-xr-k4). m=16 qkv and pooler bake only K1, because K2/K4 spill at 128 regs. qkv paths carry __launch_bounds__ minBlocks 2 (128-reg cap) so r6's 144 CTAs stay in one wave. That is 32 bake paths and 20 instances. m=32, o and the router stay r6.
target_shapes: pooler m=1 / m=8: >= 0.8 us under r6 in the bake (r6 in-prepare 18.30 / 18.56)
qkv_gate m=1/8, unpooler m=1/8 (6 MB, latency-bound: E is a bet), m=16 shapes: up to about 1 us each
kill_if: pooler m=1 E path not ≥ 0.8 µs under r6 in the same bake
local_checks: The full gv block is 99 instances and compiles in 27 s locally (nvcc 12.8, sm_90a). r6's 78 instances are SASS-identical to r6-c12. The 20 E instances have 0 spills: 119-128 regs, and 148 for the unpooler m<=8 K4 at 128 threads, which has no occupancy cap. Pooler m=1 SASS shows the bit-position chain LOP3 (lo&7), PRMT (length), SHF.R.W (lo/hi), with no LDS between consecutive position updates; the value LDS are batched after. Per unit the counts are 256 (K1), 272 (K1 rep), 279 (K2 rep) and 286 (K4 rep), and there is no LDL/STL. codec_e --test is bit-exact at ilp 1/2/4 with the negative control detected. The instruction-level emulator (proj_rsi/tools/codec_e_emu.py) is bit-exact on the reference weights for all 24 path/geometry/K combinations under early and late cp.async landing; it detects immLut 0xe4 and wait_group 4. lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9; the CPU mock of the bake builds every plan.
risks: Issue pressure: 8.0-8.9 instructions per weight. With 16 warps/SM at pooler m=1 that is about 66% of issue at the stream rate, so decode may still not be hidden at m=8/16 or on qkv.
4 B cp.async.ca is 4 LDGSTS per unit per warp, at 128 B per warp request against r6's 512 B LDG.128. LSU request rate is unmeasured.
Never executed on a GPU: the ring and prefetch are checked only by emulation (pw17's emulated kernel was bit-exact on the judge).
